ref_clues.ref_content: CONTROL: Defines the type of DMA operations (opcode: COPY, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512). Hardware handshake enable: Enable hardware handshake mode, DMA reads data from source upon input trigger. Digest swap: If 1, digest output registers are converted to big-endian byte order. Initial transfer: Marks the initial transfer to initialize DMA and SHA engine for one transfer spanning multiple DMA transfers. Abort: Aborts the DMA operation if set, sets status bit once abort complete. Go: Trigger the DMA operation when set; DMA engine clears GO automatically after configured operation complete (except for hardware handshake, where firmware must clear it).

STATUS: busy: DMA operation is active if set; cleared by DMA engine when operation complete. done: Configured DMA operation is complete; cleared automatically by hardware when starting a new transfer. aborted: Set once aborted operation drains. error: Error occurred during operation; ERROR_CODE register denotes the source. sha2_digest_valid: Indicates whether the SHA2_DIGEST register contains a valid digest; cleared on initial transfer, set when digest is written. chunk_done: Transfer of a single chunk is complete; only raised for multi-chunk memory-to-memory transfers; cleared automatically by hardware when starting a new chunk.

ref_clues.ref_content: TOTAL_DATA_SIZE: Total size (in bytes) of the data blob involved in DMA movement for multiple transfers. Minimum: 1 byte. Maximum: May be restricted to a maximum pre-defined size based on OT DMA enabled memory space allocation. Works in conjunction with Transfer width register.

CHUNK_DATA_SIZE: Size (in bytes) for a single DMA transfer. In hardware handshake mode, the DMA reads in chunks of CHUNK_DATA_SIZE from the peripheral. Minimum: 1 byte. Maximum: May be restricted to a maximum pre-defined size based on OT DMA enabled memory space allocation. Works in conjunction with Transfer width register.

FIFO address auto-increment enable: If set, consecutive 'transfer width' worth of data chunks are popped from the FIFO using consecutive register addresses; if not enabled, consecutive data chunks are popped by repeatedly reading the same register address. For writes (transmit), if set, consecutive 'transfer width' worth of data chunks are pushed to the FIFO using consecutive register addresses; if not enabled, data is written to the same register address. When enabled and the FIFO depth is reached, the FIFO address wraps back to the start address. Data buffer Auto-increment Enable: If set, data shall be loaded into consecutive buffer segments in memory, where each segment is equivalent to 'total size' worth of data. The Destination address (in receive) or Source address (in transmit) register is incremented by 'Total Size' once an equivalent amount of data is emptied/filled. If not set, the same buffer segment is overwritten or re-read each time a hardware handshake operation is triggered. All combinations of the two increment enable bits are allowed, and their interaction governs the address behavior as detailed in the appendix.
